title: Why your mind goes blank when you speak English | Words That Stick #6
description:
"I can understand 100% of the video, but when I try to speak, my mind goes blank."

Your memory isn't broken. In that moment, your brain is doing three jobs at once:
• find the word
• check if it fits
• build the grammar
…and someone is waiting.

Learning words in sentences does two of those jobs in advance. You know the word's setting, so you know it fits. You've already said it in a full sentence, so the grammar is ready. Only one job is left: find the word. And it arrives with its sentence attached: "I was swamped at work this week."

5 ways to describe that moment:
• freeze: a job interview, halfway through your answer
• draw a blank: a pub quiz, an empty answer sheet
• tongue-tied: talking to someone you like
• lose your train of thought: a story at dinner that suddenly stops
• stumble over your words: a wedding speech

You don't need a better memory. You need words that come with their sentences.

Comment the word you always forget.
